vpd.explVeryLow: A VPD of {vpd} kPa is extremely low. Mould and botrytis risk is critically high. Lower humidity immediately.
vpd.explBelow: A VPD of {vpd} kPa is below the optimum for {phase} ({min}–{max} kPa). Raise the temperature or lower humidity.
vpd.explInRange: A VPD of {vpd} kPa is within the target range for {phase} ({min}–{max} kPa). Stomata open, transpiration and nutrient uptake optimal.
vpd.explAbove: A VPD of {vpd} kPa exceeds the optimal range for {phase} ({min}–{max} kPa). Raise humidity or lower the temperature.
vpd.explCritical: A VPD of {vpd} kPa is critically high. The plant closes its stomata — growth and transpiration stop. Correct the climate urgently.
vpd.explTargetRh: To reach the ideal VPD of {mid} kPa, humidity should be around {rh}%.
vpd.explSvpAir: Saturation vapour pressure at {temp} °C air temperature.
vpd.explSvpLeaf: Saturation vapour pressure at {temp} °C leaf temperature ({offset} °C offset).

lighting.explPpfdLow: Well below the target range ({target}). Move the lamp closer or use a stronger model.
lighting.explPpfdHigh: Above the recommended range ({target}). Without CO₂ enrichment, light saturation starts around ~900–1,000 µmol/m²/s, with bleaching risk above that — increase the distance or dim.
lighting.explHeightFactor: At {height} cm mounting height, roughly {pct}% of the light reaches the canopy.

nutrients.explDosage: For {product} at a target EC of {ec} mS/cm in {phase}.
nutrients.tipCoco: Coco: plan for a 10–20% drain rate to avoid salt build-up.
nutrients.tipHydro: Hydro: fully replace the nutrient solution every 5–7 days.
nutrients.tipErde: Soil: organic buffering can absorb EC spikes.

ventilation.explVolGelb: Tight — going one size larger is recommended.
ventilation.explVolRot: High demand — use a powerful fan with a speed controller.
ventilation.explHeatLoad: {watts} W generate roughly {btu} BTU/h of heat input.

yield.explTotal: Real yields vary by ±30%. This estimate is a rough guide.

tool.categoryDescKlima: Calculate VPD, airflow demand and duct diameter — so temperature, VPD and humidity match every stage.
tool.categoryDescLicht: Find the optimal light intensity (PPFD) and daily light integral (DLI).
tool.categoryDescNaehrstoffe: Calculate target EC and dosage — for every stage and substrate.
tool.categoryDescPlanung: Estimate your yield realistically before you start the grow.

ventilation.tip1: Buy a fan one size up — it runs quieter and lasts longer.
ventilation.tip2: Every 90° bend in your ducting costs ~10% of the airflow.
ventilation.tip3: A speed controller lets you fine-tune temperature and noise.
ventilation.tip4: A carbon filter noticeably increases resistance. +25% is a realistic guide, but it can be more.
ventilation.roomHint: Enter all dimensions as interior measurements in metres.
ventilation.akfHint: Increases resistance — you need roughly 25% more airflow
ventilation.interpSmall: A compact inline fan is enough for your {vol} m³ room.
ventilation.interpMid: Medium demand — a good 125 or 150 mm fan will do.
ventilation.interpLarge: High demand — look for an EC fan with a speed controller.
ventilation.recLarge: Pick an EC fan that still moves your airflow at 80% speed.
ventilation.recDuct: Duct diameter {mm} mm — going one size up never hurts.

nutrients.tip1: Calibrate your EC meter regularly — a ±0.3 error makes a difference to plants.
nutrients.tip2: With coco, always add CalMag — coco actively binds calcium and magnesium.
nutrients.tip3: Drain EC well above input EC (>+0.5)? Flush with plain water.
nutrients.tip4: High temperatures → plants drink more than they feed → EC in the substrate rises.
nutrients.solutionHint: Base dosage is on the product — or use 2.0 ml/L as a starting point.
nutrients.waterHint: Total volume of the nutrient solution
nutrients.baseDosageHint: Manufacturer figure or your own experience
nutrients.interpLowEc: Your tap water is already mineral-rich — little nutrient needed.
nutrients.interpLowDose: Very low dose. Start here and increase gradually.
nutrients.interpNormal: For {liters} L of nutrient solution to EC {ec} mS/cm.
nutrients.recSplit: Split the dose in two and check pH after each step.
nutrients.recDrain: Measure drain EC regularly — salt build-up is more likely here.

yield.tip1: In practice this estimate varies by ±30% — treat it as a planning basis, not a promise.
yield.tip2: Indoor target: 0.5 g/W is realistic for beginners. 1 g/W and above needs optimal conditions.
yield.tip3: Autoflower: shorter cycle, but less control over when flowering starts.
yield.tip4: Hydro only pays off once you reliably control EC, pH and temperature.
yield.setupHint: The more precise your inputs, the better the forecast.
yield.potNote: Root space is the single biggest factor for outdoor yield — a bigger pot beats experience.
yield.interpLow: {perPlant} g/plant is a typical beginner figure. Plenty of room to improve.
yield.interpMid: A solid figure. A better veg phase and optimised nutrients can raise it considerably.
yield.interpHigh: Strong forecast. This needs precise control over light, climate and nutrients.
yield.recLow: Check light and nutrients first — that has the biggest effect.
yield.recHigh: This figure is possible under ideal conditions — plan with 60–70% as a safe value.

lighting.tip1: Measure PPFD with a PAR meter — calculations are always estimates.
lighting.tip2: Above 1,000 µmol/m²/s, CO₂ supplementation almost always pays off.
lighting.tip3: DLI above 45 mol/m²/d without CO₂ usually causes light stress rather than more yield.
lighting.tip4: Modern top LEDs reach 2.8–3.2 µmol/J. Standard LEDs sit at 2.0–2.5 µmol/J.
lighting.situationHint: Adjust the values to your setup — the results update instantly.
lighting.interpVeryLow: Too little light — plants grow very slowly.
lighting.interpLow: Enough for seedlings and clones, but below the veg optimum.
lighting.interpVeg: Good range for the vegetative phase. DLI: {dli} mol/m²/d.
lighting.interpFlower: Optimal for flowering. DLI: {dli} mol/m²/d — great.
lighting.interpVeryHigh: Very intense lighting — CO₂ and precise temperature control required.
lighting.recLow: Hang the lamp lower or use a stronger fixture.
lighting.recHigh: Increase the lamp distance or add CO₂ to 1,000–1,200 ppm.

vpd.tip1: Leaf temperature is decisive — LED lamps keep leaves roughly 1–3 °C cooler than the room air.
vpd.tip2: High VPD in flower (0.8–1.5 kPa) boosts terpene production and firms up buds.
vpd.tip3: VPD below 0.4 kPa raises botrytis risk sharply — especially in dense canopies.
vpd.tip4: Change VPD gradually at stage transitions: don't jump straight from seedling VPD to flowering VPD.
vpd.tip5: Good air circulation effectively lowers leaf temperature and with it the VPD.
vpd.climateHint: Adjust temperature and humidity — the VPD updates instantly.
vpd.interpGreen: Perfect conditions for {phase}. Stomata are open, transpiration and nutrient uptake are optimal.
vpd.interpBelow: VPD {diff} kPa below the target range — lower humidity {urgency} or raise the temperature.
vpd.interpAbove: VPD {diff} kPa above the target range — raise humidity or lower the temperature to avoid drought stress.
